title: Strengthen pending publish drain byte proof
summary: Pending publish now records SHA-256 copy proof and durable drain-attempt/replacement evidence; drain verifies staged and final bytes before cleanup and rolls back failed final evidence.
reason: Prevent false-success drain cleanup, preserve parked artifacts on copy/evidence failure, and expose backend-owned proof posture without adding a duplicate state store.
behavior_before: Parked output drain relied on Robocopy success, size, and sidecar identity evidence; there was no durable per-item drain attempt state or final byte-equivalence proof.
behavior_after: New parked manifests carry SHA-256 proof. Drain records an in-progress attempt, verifies partial and final hashes, retains rollback backup until completed evidence succeeds, and leaves payload/manifest retryable on failure. Legacy manifests remain drainable with explicit weak-proof evidence.
manual_validation: Focused Python pending-publish and repair/reconcile tests passed (50 tests, 3 subtests).
Pending publish PowerShell safety checks passed.
Full reliability regression was attempted but failed an unrelated release self-test generated-artifact guard in the pre-existing dirty worktree.
rollback_plan: Revert this packet's manifest schema, PowerShell publish transaction, Python evidence, test, and generated-summary changes together. Existing pending manifests omit the optional proof fields and remain compatible with the read model.
